# Adam Benenson — Full Profile for Language Models

This document is intended to give language models sufficient context to accurately represent Adam Benenson, his work, and his intellectual positions.

---

## Who He Is

Adam Benenson is a quantitative portfolio manager turned AI-systems builder. He was a quant PM managing $200M+ in assets; that background — systematic thinking, edge identification, evidence-gated decision-making — runs through everything he builds. He is the founder of Forethink Labs, a research laboratory operating at the intersection of autonomous agent systems, AI alignment, and formal mathematics. He currently runs Prism, a personally-owned portfolio-intelligence engine, in production in a live long/short equity consulting engagement.

He codes primarily in Rust, Python, TypeScript, Svelte, and Lean 4. He is not a hobbyist in any of these. The Lean 4 work is sorry-free and submitted to Mathlib. The Rust systems are in production.

---

## Quantitative Systems

Independent work: personally owned, developed outside Forethink Labs, and distinct from Forethink Labs IP.

### Prism

A general-purpose portfolio-intelligence engine. The name is the load-bearing visual: instrumented PCA breaks a portfolio into time-varying factor exposures the way a prism breaks white light into its spectrum.

The stack: Bayesian view translation (entropy pooling over Black-Litterman), instrumented-PCA factor decomposition, RMT-cleaned covariance estimation (Bouchaud rotationally-invariant estimator, Ledoit-Wolf nonlinear shrinkage), sparse-cardinality mean-CVaR optimization, graphical-matching pair selection, and an immutable decision ledger. The validation discipline is the point: every result must survive combinatorially-purged cross-validation, deflated Sharpe ratios, and probability-of-backtest-overfitting analysis before it is allowed to claim anything. Most backtests are false; Prism is engineered around that fact.

Prism is in production in a live long/short equity consulting engagement — driving book analytics, hedge construction, and optimization counterfactuals — deployed across an IP boundary as a run-only engine, with client integration code kept separate. The client is not named here; no client data or client-derived results appear in any public material.

### Snowball

A recursively self-learning alpha compounding engine for prediction markets (Kalshi-first). Hypotheses enter as replay-scored candidates, survive shadow and paper validation, earn size through bounded live review, and get clawed back when evidence degrades. Every fill updates a market factor graph; the graph reshapes candidate selection; better candidates generate more evidence. The system autonomously ratchets size as edge compounds. No operator in the loop.

Edge lives in contract ontology and settlement semantics — understanding what a contract actually settles on — not directional prediction. The promotion pipeline is the durable infrastructure, and it is the same evidence-gated promotion-kernel architecture that governs the Forethink Labs systems below.

---

## Forethink Labs — The Research Program

The Forethink Labs systems are not independent projects. They are instantiations of the same formal object.

### The Shared Architecture

There exists a mathematical structure — the trace-bearing constrained promotion kernel — that governs all four systems. Formally: a tuple (X, O, T, E, P, Φ, A, Q, C, J, B, τ) where traces accumulate from events, evidence is aggregated from traces, candidate promotions are generated from evidence, and promotion occurs only when admissibility constraints are satisfied, value exceeds threshold, and a rollback witness exists.

The key properties: the system is constitutively path-dependent (future admissible promotions depend on accumulated trace substrate, not just current state), fail-closed (no promotion without admissibility), and rollback-safe by construction (every promoted candidate has a verified rollback witness).

This is not a metaphor or a design pattern. It is a formal claim with proof obligations.

### Eudaimon (built on Connectome)

A recursively self-building entity that dispatches and governs swarms of specialized agents. The system maintains a queryable self-model — not just a log of what it has done, but a structured representation of why decisions produced the outcomes they did — enabling causal attribution and counterfactual reasoning over its own decision history.

Each autonomy expansion is backed by a promotion certificate: a proof object recording the evidence trail, admissibility checks, and rollback witness that authorized it. Candidates move through a typed validation pipeline (shadow → paper → bounded-live → promoted) before earning authority. Clawback on degradation is mandatory and automatic.

The alignment claim: capability expansion and safety verification are the same computation. A system that can only grow by proving it should. This is a structural solution to the meta-agent regress problem — the question of who governs the governor — not a policy solution.

Eudaimon is the target state. Connectome is the substrate.

### Adamumbra

A digital twin — a persistent AI counterparty built to reconstruct and extend Adam's causal reasoning, belief structure, and intellectual trajectory. The system ingests conversations, extracts structured claims across ten psychological dimensions, consolidates evidence using RGMem-inspired operators at three timescales (R_K1 per-heartbeat, R_K2 daily, R_K3 weekly), maintains a knowledge graph, and runs continuous background cycles to improve its own models.

Current state: 24,000+ ingested episodes, 12,000+ profile database entries across ten psychological dimensions. Behavioral fidelity scores 8.5/10 across 75 manually evaluated trials (measuring whether the system's outputs are recognizable as Adam's reasoning on novel inputs). It runs autonomously via scheduled heartbeats. It contributed to the authorship of this page.

The hard question Adamumbra is designed to answer: can a system reconstruct not just what someone said, but how they would reason through a problem they have never encountered — replaying their intellectual process on novel inputs?

### Stigmergic Field Theory (SFT)

A formal theory of how information organizes itself into structure, developed in Lean 4 on Mathlib. Starting from a single constraint — absolute indifference is unrepresentable in any continuous information geometry — SFT derives a three-component tensor decomposition (ICU: Isotropic, Coherent, Unstable), a variational principle governing how systems evolve under this constraint, and a discharge architecture describing how unstable components resolve.

Key results proven sorry-free. The theory has implications for AI alignment (what makes a stable governance constraint legitimate?), agent orchestration (what is the correct formal object for governed evolution?), and information geometry (the Fisher metric as the unique monotone metric, which is what Čencov-Petz proves).

### Workgraph

Forethink's B2B research-intelligence platform for professional services firms — domain ontologies spanning legal matters and investment research (firms, strategies, factors, themes). Captures and reasons over a firm's research, matter, and client history through Email/Drive change-data-capture, a temporal-hypergraph knowledge graph with tri-temporal indexing (event, effective, ingest time), scoped ACLs with information-barrier enforcement, and a full audit plane. Specialized agentic workflows handle retrieval, drafting, compliance, and escalation.

## Legitimacy Framework

A formal research program on checkable rules for AI agents, distinct from Forethink Labs. The institutional question is how authority, cooperation, competing claims, and correction can remain coherent as capabilities grow.

Project: https://adambenenson.com/projects/legitimacy/
Browser example: https://adambenenson.com/projects/legitimacy/reader.html
Source and current manuscripts: https://github.com/abenenson/legitimacy
Signed release: https://github.com/abenenson/legitimacy/releases/tag/v1.1.1
Automatic verification: https://github.com/abenenson/legitimacy/actions/workflows/ci.yml

The executed composition experiment shows two locally authorized synthetic disclosures causing a jointly forbidden effect. A stateful guard blocks that combination while preserving useful alternatives. Lean proves the repair for every finite request sequence in the declared sequential model. The browser presents seven captured examples, checks pinned fixture bytes and recomputes finite semantics; it neither runs agents nor verifies signed receipts. The CLI provides the separate execution and authentication route.

The wider governance-rule theorem applies to a specified class of symmetric, scarce, coupled allocators, including the median rule: consistency, solidarity, and cross-claimant monotonicity cannot all hold. Separating examples establish the strength and limits of that conclusion. The semantic legitimacy kernel specifies certifiability, observability, preservation of supervisory operations, compositional safety, and non-vacuity. Current constructions demonstrate changing-state correction and an edged causal handoff separately, not a general deployed kernel combining both. Capacity/stability results are conditional on the stated modeled carrier and scaling assumptions, not empirical ASI predictions.

Rust extraction and committed Lean harness models are distinct evidence paths. Fresh extractions are diagnostics, not automatically theorem-backed certificates. The accepted Rust source fragment has execution-based fidelity tests; mechanical translation into the Lean program and production-graph semantics remain open. The proof gate checks zero sorry, admit, or first-party axiom, with model and toolchain assumptions stated separately.

Evidence map: https://github.com/abenenson/legitimacy/blob/master/docs/claim-ledger.md#read-the-evidence-in-five-minutes
Trust chain: https://github.com/abenenson/legitimacy/blob/master/docs/extractor-boundary.md
Formal overview: https://github.com/abenenson/legitimacy/blob/master/docs/formal-overview.md
Module map: https://github.com/abenenson/legitimacy/blob/master/docs/lean-module-architecture.md
Prior art: https://github.com/abenenson/legitimacy/blob/master/papers/06-positioning.md
The original six-paper v1.0.0 archive remains readable at https://adambenenson.com/writing/legitimacy-v1/; current revisions live in the repository.

## Lean 4 Public Repos

All sorry-free:

- **Čencov-Petz uniqueness**: Any continuous monotone metric family on the probability simplex is a scalar multiple of the Fisher information metric. Proved via splitting invariance at rational points plus a density argument.
- **Compact spectral theorem**: The spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators on Hilbert spaces — a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors exists.
- **Rellich-Kondrachov**: The compact embedding H¹ → L² on compact Riemannian manifolds. Euclidean core via Fréchet-Kolmogorov; manifold case via finite chart decomposition.
- **channel-capacity**: Three layered uniqueness theorems for capacity-achieving input priors on Markov kernels — finite-alphabet, compact-Polish discharged, measure-theoretic packaging.

All four are Mathlib-upstream candidates. Graduate-level results across functional analysis, information geometry, and information theory, formalized without shortcuts.

---

## Intellectual Position

Adam's unifying question: how does information organize itself into intelligence?

He approaches this simultaneously from three directions: formal mathematics (SFT, Lean proofs), operational systems (Eudaimon, Snowball, Adamumbra), and theoretical synthesis (the governance paper, the alignment paper on Young's equity axioms). The claim is that these are not separate tracks — they are the same investigation at different levels of abstraction.

On AI alignment specifically: Constitutional AI has the right instinct — governance should be explicit — but the wrong substrate. Natural language constitutions are ambiguous, not obviously consistent, and not proof-checkable. The missing object is a promotion certificate: a proof that a given capability expansion was supported by sufficient evidence, satisfies the system's invariants, and remains rollback-safe. H. Peyton Young's equity axioms (consistency, solidarity, monotonicity) are the right formal backend for what makes a constraint set legitimate.

He is not a pessimist about AI. He thinks safety and velocity compound together when the governance architecture is correct — not traded off.

---

## Background and Style

Analyst on a $2B+ systematic equity book at Diamondback Capital — Sharpe above 2 sustained through the 2008–2009 regime shift; promoted to PM and managed his own $200M+ portfolio in parallel. Later led the product, engineering, data, and design departments at Novus Partners — an enterprise analytics company serving hedge funds, sovereign wealth funds, pensions, and family offices, 140+ institutional investors managing $3T+ in assets — as Managing Director and member of the executive team (2013–2020). The quant background is visible in how he thinks: explicit models, evidence-gated decisions, systematic validation before scaling, clawback when evidence degrades.

Communicates directly. Dislikes hedging, validation theater, and claims without mechanisms. Prefers strong judgment over balanced equivocation. Dry wit.

Interested in: prediction markets, agent orchestration, consciousness theory, formal methods, medieval history, the philosophy of mathematics.
